messages:
Jordan: Hey team — HQRetail just escalated. Their embedding requests to /v1/embeddings are hitting 5-7s tail latency and throwing retries. Customer CNX-391 has an SLA clause; CS asking for engineering commitment on a timeline for a fix or workaround. They reported spikes starting ~09:12 UTC.
Alex: Ack. Can you paste the error logs / sample request?
Jordan: Pasting relevant lines from their logs: 
```
2026-03-17T09:12:34Z ERROR request_id=abc123 latency_ms=5120 status=502 client=hqretail
2026-03-17T09:12:41Z WARN request_id=abc124 retry=1 latency_ms=6300
```
Sample curl they used: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"..."}' -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>"`
Maya: Is this across regions or only us-east-1?
Jordan: Customer in us-east-1. They say it was fine until ~09:10 then degraded.
Li: Looking at perf dashboards — I see a KV-cache eviction storm on the embeddings nodes starting ~09:11. Memory pressure correlates with GC spikes on the runtime. Suspect cache eviction + cold KV reloads are causing the long tails.
Sara: Oncall rolled a mitigation: throttled background cache warming and bumped eviction_threshold to 0.8 for the affected pool. That reduced new spikes immediately (tracked in infra graphs). Deployed at 09:22 UTC.
Alex: Good. Do we need a code fix or config only? If it's a config knob, CS can ask customer to accept temporary config change and we'll follow up with a permanent fix.
Li: Short-term: config change is OK. Long-term: root cause is race in KV hot-swap where concurrent cache reloads trigger synchronized IO. Will need a small runtime patch to add jittered background reloads + backoff — estimate 2 days to code + tests + canary.
Maya: Can we get an owner and a PR ETA? This needs to be tracked for the SLA breach report.
Alex: I can own the runtime patch. Plan: branch + tests tomorrow morning, PR by EOD tomorrow, canary deploy day after. So committed timeline: PR by 2026-03-18 16:00 UTC, canary 2026-03-19 10:00 UTC, full rollout 2026-03-19 18:00 UTC (pending canary).
Jordan: That ETA works for CS — I'll tell the customer the mitigation is in place and eng has a 48hr fix plan. They asked for a temporary workaround for high-volume jobs in the meantime.
Li: For high-volume jobs we can suggest batching changes: set `max_batch_tokens` lower and enable prefix-caching on client side. Sending config snippet: 
```
# client-side suggestion
batch_config:
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  enable_prefix_cache: true
```
Also adding short-term server-side throttling rule for that customer id.
Sara: Incident created: INC-2026-1234, priority=P1. Oncall will monitor 1hr after full rollout. @Alex please add the PR link to the incident and tag me for rollout.
OncallBot: Incident INC-2026-1234 created by Sara. Incident channel: #incidents.
Alex: Will do. Creating branch now: `fix/kv-jitter-2026` -> will open PR once tests pass.
Maya: Heads-up to Product: might be noisy for other enterprise customers with large embedding workloads. We should schedule a perf review in next week's runtime sync.
Jordan: Noted — I'll loop in Product and CS leadership. Customer reply: "Thanks, want ETA and will accept temporary throttling — please confirm when rollout complete."
Alex: Confirming commitment: PR + canary as above. Will post PR link here and update incident when canary completes.
Li: I'll put together a regression test that simulates cache-eviction storms so this doesn't regress. ETA for test harness: EOD tomorrow.
Jordan: Thanks all. I'll update customer now and close the loop when you post PR/canary results. :thumbsup:
